title: Some prayers even ask the saints to act by their own delegated power and command
source_text: XCIV. Adde quod in usu Ecclesiae Romanae non paucae preces ad Sanctos directae reperiuntur, in quibus ab ipsis non solum postulantur bona Gratiae & Gloriae, sed etiam rogantur ut ea nobis praestent tradita sibi potestate, & jussu ac praecepto suo. Quod plane aliud est quam ejusmodi bona suis orationibus nobis a Deo impetrare. Veluti quum Apostolis in communi dicitur, Qui caelum verbo clauditis, Serasque ejus solvitis, Nos a peccatis omnibus, Solvite jussu quaesumus. Quorum praecepto subditur, Salus & languor omnium, Sanate aegros moribus, Nos reddentes virtutibus. Item, Nos a reatu noxios, Solvi jubete quaesumus. Et speciatim ad Petrum Apostolum, Peccati vincula Resolve tibi potestate tradita, Qua cunctis caelum Verbo claudis, aperis. Ut supra quoque fusius a nobis probatum est.
pass_a_gloss: Add that in the usage of the Roman Church not a few prayers directed to the Saints are found, in which not only are goods of Grace and Glory asked of them, but they are also asked that they furnish them to us by the power handed over to them, and by their command and precept. Which is plainly another thing than to obtain such goods for us from God by their prayers. As when it is said to the Apostles in common, You who shut heaven by a word, And loose its bolts, Loose us from all sins, By your command, we beseech. To whose precept is subjected, Health and sickness of all, Heal those sick in morals, Restoring us to virtues. Again, Order us guilty, we beseech, To be loosed from guilt. And specially to the Apostle Peter, Loose the chains of sin By the power handed to thee, By which thou shuttest heaven to all by a Word, and openest. As was also proved more fully by us above.
pass_b_english: Besides, in the usage of the Roman Church there are quite a few prayers addressed to the saints in which they are asked not only for the goods of grace and glory, but also to give these to us by the power entrusted to them, by their own order and command. That is plainly something other than obtaining such goods for us from God by their prayers.

So the apostles together are addressed: "You who shut heaven by your word and loose its bolts, loose us from all our sins by your command, we pray." And: "Health and sickness of all are subject to your command; heal those sick in their ways, restoring us to virtue." And again: "Command that we, guilty men, be loosed from our guilt, we pray." And to the Apostle Peter in particular: "By the power given you, loose the chains of sin, you who by your word shut heaven to all and open it."
We proved this more fully above as well.

choices.term: Quorum praecepto subditur, Salus & languor omnium
choices.english: Health and sickness of all are subject to your command
choices.why: Subditur is the verb of the hymn line; the English joins it to its subject as the hymn does.
rejected: It is added by their precept
